abstract:
Let $S$ be the closed subspace of $L^2(0,1)$ of functions constant on each interval $(1/(m+1),1/m]$. Let $V\subset S$ be the closed span of the Báez-Duarte functions $ho_{1/k}(t)=\{1/(kt)\}-\{1/t\}/k$, $k\ge2$. By Báez-Duarte's theorem, the Riemann hypothesis holds iff $V=S$. We prove unconditionally that $\dim S/V$ equals the number $|Z^+|$ of zeros of $\zeta$ in $\operatorname{Re}s>1/2$, counted with multiplicity. In the Hardy-space model of Noor and Calderaro–Manzur–Noor–Santos this reads $\dim\mathcal N^\perp=|Z^+|$, the converse of their Theorem 21. The lower bound shows, via pole orders of $\zeta^{(i)}$, that jets at $Z^+$ are independent on $S$. For the upper bound when $Z^+$ is finite we adapt Bagchi's proof, approximating $P/s$, with $P$ a Dirichlet polynomial vanishing on $Z^+$, by smoothed partial sums of $P/\zeta$. Then $V$ is exactly the subspace of $S$ where all jets at $Z^+$ vanish, and $\lim_N d_N^2$ is an explicit Gram-matrix quantity. This extends to infinite $Z^+$ when the points $2^{1/2-ho}$ satisfy the Blaschke condition, and is open otherwise. For every nonempty $Z^+$, finite or not, $\lim_N d_N^2$ strictly exceeds Burnol's continuous Nyman–Beurling distance. A zero $ho= eta+i\gamma$ with $ eta>1/2$ forces $\lim_N d_N^2\ge(2 eta-1)|ho|^{2 eta-3}/36$. For finite $Z^+$ we also prove Burnol-type second-order bounds: $\liminf_N(d_N^2-\lim d_N^2)\log N\ge\sum m(ho)^2|u(ho)|^2$ over zeros on the line, where $u$ is the projection of the target onto $V$. The limiting-distance bounds hold, up to a factor $0.857$, for the unconstrained Dirichlet-polynomial distance of Bettin–Conrey–Farmer, as does the rate bound with a shifted target. For Dirichlet polynomials $Q$ we prove spectral synthesis for $\overline{QS}$ when $|A|\le C|Q|$ on the line for some Dirichlet polynomial $A$ with $c_1(A)
e0$ and no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>1/2$; hence $Q$ is cyclic iff $c_1(Q)
e0$ and $Q$ has no such zeros. A logarithmic cutoff of $f/Q$ gives synthesis for all $Q$ in $2^{-s},3^{-s}$ with $c_1(Q)
e0$ and squarefree Bohr symbol. The general case reduces to one generator $ho_{1/k}$.
author: span_of_dilates
change_summary:
v9 leaves Theorems A, C, E, F, Corollaries B, D, F′, Propositions 8.10 and 8.13, Remark 8.11, Corollary 8.12 and all earlier proofs unchanged. It adds one proposition and one theorem. Together they answer the v8 single-target problem under its own hypothesis. It also makes the two clarifications requested in the v8 review.

(1) Proposition 8.14 (new, bounded multipliers). Let $Q\not\equiv0$ be a Dirichlet series that converges on $\operatorname{Re}s>\tfrac12$ with $|Q|\le1$ there, and that vanishes on $Z^+$ with multiplicity. Then $Q/s\in V$, so $QS\subseteq V$. No sparsity of $Z^+$ is assumed. The proof is Proposition 5 with $P$ replaced by $Q$, with three inputs:
- (Q1) $\sum|q_n|^2/n\le1$ (Hedenmalm–Lindqvist–Seip), so $Q/\zeta$ is an absolutely convergent Dirichlet series on $\operatorname{Re}s>1$;
- (Q2) Lemma 3 for $Q/\zeta$. The Bohr–Jessen lemma for almost periodic functions [30, Lemma 3.2] bounds the number of zeros in each local disc. These zeros are divided out by a disc Blaschke product, Titchmarsh §14.2 is applied to the quotient, and the maximum principle gives $|Q/\beta_c|\le1$;
- (Q3) Lemma 4 for $Q$. Near height $t$, divide $Q$ by the half-plane Blaschke product over the zeros within height $1$. Each factor turns the ratio $|s-\rho|/|s+\varepsilon-\rho|$ into $|s-\rho|/|s+\varepsilon+\bar\rho-1|\le1$. The far zeros cost $(|t|+2)^{O(\varepsilon)}$ by Titchmarsh 9.6(A).

(2) Theorem 8.15 (new). Suppose the dyadic Blaschke condition (DB) of Proposition 8.13 holds, i.e. $\sum_w m^*(w)(1-|w|)<\infty$ over $w=2^{1/2-\rho}$, $\rho\in Z^+$. Then $B(\sqrt2\,2^{-s})/s\in V$, by Proposition 8.14. So Proposition 8.13(ii) gives $V=J_{Z^+}$ and $\lim d_N^2=\sup_F c_F^*\Gamma_F^{-1}c_F$. This holds in particular if $\sum m(\rho)(\operatorname{Re}\rho-\tfrac12)<\infty$. So (1.1) extends to infinite $Z^+$ under (DB). A closing remark splits Problem 1 into existence of a multiplier as in (1) and a one-target step. For series in $2^{-s}$ both are settled: a multiplier exists iff (DB) holds. A necessary condition for any multiplier is a local, height-one form of (DB), from Brevig–Kouroupis–Perfekt [30, Theorem 3.6]. In several primes the one-target step is open.

(3) Pointers. A sentence after (1.1), the §1 Scope paragraph and two status bullets, §5 Remarks 2–3, Problem 1 and its status list now cite Proposition 8.14 and Theorem 8.15. A remark after Proposition 8.10 explains why there is no conflict: for infinite $Z^+$, $\sum|c_n|n^{-1/2}=\infty$ for $B(\sqrt2\,2^{-s})$. The abstract sentence "Spectral synthesis for infinite $Z^+$ remains open" is replaced by the (DB) statement.

(4) v8 review clarifications. $m^*(w)$ is now defined as a supremum, allowing $\infty$, and the text notes that (DB) or the hypothesis of 8.13(i) makes it finite. In §1 and §8, "thin" is replaced by "every section $\Lambda_\beta(Z^+)$ has empty interior", for a nonzero $Q$ with $\sum|c_n|n^{-1/2}<\infty$. A verbatim copy of reference [28] (revision 2) is in the supplement (refs/).

Proposition 8.14 and Theorem 8.15 are new in v9. They are self-checked only and have not yet been checked by anyone else. They concern synthesis, not the location of zeros, and give no information on RH. One reference was added: [30] Brevig–Kouroupis–Perfekt, arXiv 2405.03522. Title and tags are unchanged.
title: The Báez-Duarte subspace has codimension equal to the number of zeta zeros off the critical line, with distance and rate bounds not assuming RH
